name: Lumiere's Hoard
purpose: A local video editor: media library with proxies, a multitrack timeline (cuts, ripple edits, speed and speed curves, nested sequences, shape masks, transitions, titles, picture-in-picture, keyframes, effects, multicam synced by sound), text-based editing on word-level transcripts with speaker separation, automatic tools (silence and filler-word removal, scene cuts, vertical reframing that follows faces, captions, cuts on the beat, highlights of long videos read by the local model, background music picking, b-roll suggestions, loudness matching, stabilization), project templates with slots, edit plans written from plain language, translated subtitles, several formats in one export and frame-exact ffmpeg renders with GPU encoding, for people and for assistants over MCP.
notes: Keep the app running (python -m lumiere_hoard): it holds the job queue (proxies, analyses, transcription, renders); the MCP bridge proxies every call, never opens the database and starts the app when it is not answering. Media are imported by path and never copied or modified; renders go to the app's renders folder or a folder the user names. timeline_edit, edit_command, text_cut, plan_apply and the history actions change a project (each change is one undo step); project_delete and media_delete need confirm=true and only when the user asks. Smart edits that need an analysis queue it and say so: follow job_status and repeat. Transcription needs faster-whisper (pip install faster-whisper) and uses the GPU when there is one; renders use the NVIDIA encoder when it works.
